name: OpenDisplay
use_label: iPad or iPhone as a Mac second monitor
one_liner: Turns an iPhone or iPad into a real second monitor for a Mac.

text.why: Adding one more screen to a Mac usually starts with buying a device or paying for an app. opendisplay connects an iPhone or iPad you already own over USB or WiFi and uses it as a second monitor. It states low-latency H.264, Retina HiDPI and touch input. Written in Swift and published under GPL-3.0.
text.take: Turns an iPhone or iPad you already own into a true extended display with no account or dongle.
build: A portable setup that adds a second screen in a meeting room
A desk layout with the iPad kept for tool panels only

who.situation: adds a second screen in a meeting room or café
wants a second monitor without a paid app
keeps the iPad for docs and tool panels only

start.text: Mac: open OpenDisplay.dmg from the latest release, drag to Applications (macOS 14+)
iPhone/iPad: install the app via the TestFlight public beta (iOS 16+)
Connect a data-capable USB cable, then allow Screen Recording and Accessibility

caveat: Uses the private CGVirtualDisplay API, so a macOS update may break it
The iOS app installs via TestFlight or your own build, not the App Store
Encrypted WiFi transport is still on the roadmap

license.scope_text: Use freely. Release your source if you redistribute (copyleft).
